address: Quellijnstraat 36, Amsterdam-Zuid (Weteringbuurt / Quellijnkwartier): 1927 brick block of the Amsterdam School period, a three- to five-storey north front with arched timber garage gates at ground level and a rounded corner, and a long three-storey canal front of small banded windows carrying the green Heineken name
notes: Quellijnstraat 36 (BAG pand 0363100012098847, built 1927, 220 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof max 17.1 m): a large 1920s brick block of the Quellijnkwartier with several wings round courtyards. Photographed: the 55 m north front (w01-6: brick with horizontal bands, a rounded corner at the left, three tall arched timber gates, a green door and a ground-floor playground), the 52 m west front on the canal (w02-268: three storeys of small windows in brick bands, a green HEINEKEN name, large dark openings at the right) and corner details on the east (w03-340, w04-186, w05-186). The identification as an Amsterdam School period block comes from the BAG year and the photographed brick bands and arched gates.

walls[0] = panel 42 (N, 27 m, eaves 11.6; surface 51): 3 storeys x 6 bays with string courses and three garage doors on the ground. walls[1] = panel 51 (N, 28 m, eaves 15.0; surfaces 60, 216): 4 storeys x 6 bays with string courses. walls[2] = panel 70 (W, 52 m, eaves 10.0; surfaces 90, 91): 3 storeys x 13 bays of small windows (storey 3, the strip of the 11.9 m gable above the 10.0 m eaves, is blank: a window there overlapped the wall) with string courses and the HEINEKEN name letters on a cornice band (in the photograph the name sits in the middle of the wall, not on a cornice). Simplified: the gates are plain tall doors without arched heads, the rounded corner is 3DBAG facets, the green door and the ground-floor playground are not modelled. Not drawn: the east wings with the corner details, the courtyard walls and the 17 m rear blocks (blank brick).
